context: Depends on one-engine-unify-statistics for the underlying metric computation. Characterize current classifications on fixtures; unify defaults (decide: keep MCP's ladder as the canonical severity taxonomy, keep CLI's threshold override semantics); migrate the three call sites; add a parity test asserting all three surfaces classify a shared fixture identically. Also migrate MCP's _classify_query_changes (analytics.py:484-530) and _compute_trend_direction onto the core policy.
description: Three inconsistent regression/trend policies answer the same question today: CLI compare's threshold + exit-code logic (benchbox/cli/commands/compare.py:1116-1128, :1333-1373), report's hardcoded -5% IMPROVED cutoff (benchbox/cli/commands/report.py:186-191), and MCP's severity ladder critical>=100%/high>=50%/medium>=25%/low (benchbox/mcp/tools/analytics.py:920-929) plus +/-5% trend thresholds (analytics.py:618-633). An agent via MCP and a human via CLI can reach different regression verdicts from the same files. Create one core policy module (thresholds, severity ladder, trend classification, improved cutoff) with a single set of defaults; all three call sites consume it. Caller-supplied thresholds (CLI --fail-on-regression / threshold_percent MCP param) remain as overrides mapping onto the same core defaults.

anti_patterns.dont: average the three policies into new blended thresholds
anti_patterns.instead: pick one canonical policy and document the choice in the core module + ADR reference
anti_patterns.why: a fourth policy is worse than any of the three

anti_patterns.dont: hardcode display-layer cutoffs (report's -5% IMPROVED) in the command file again
anti_patterns.instead: expose it as a named core constant the display imports
anti_patterns.why: display constants are policy too; that is how this drift started

preserves.behavior: CLI compare's --fail-on-regression exit-code contract (non-zero on regression) is unchanged for scripts that depend on it.
MCP analyze_results response schema keeps its field names; only the numbers' provenance moves to core.
report's DB-backed detect_regressions API keeps its signature.

prior_art.concept: ResultDatabase.detect_regressions already exists as a core regression entry point for report
Severity ladder and trend thresholds to be relocated, not reinvented

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit -k 'regression and parity' -q
verifications.description: Three-surface classification parity on shared fixtures
verifications.expected: compare, report, and MCP analytics classify a shared fixture identically.

verifications.description: No local severity/trend constants remain in surface layers
verifications.expected: Severity and trend policy live only in core.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/cli -k 'fail_on_regression or regression_exit' -q

work_units.evidence: Re-verified at HEAD and found a FOURTH policy site the review missed: benchbox/core/results/database.py:898 hardcodes is_regression = change > 10, and detect_regressions then requires BOTH that flag and change_pct > threshold_pct, so any --threshold below 10 was silently inert (a 7% slowdown could never be reported at --threshold 5). Characterized all four on a shared delta matrix including every band boundary.
work_units.summary: Re-verify the three policies at HEAD; characterize classifications on shared fixtures

work_units.evidence: benchbox/core/results/regression_policy.py: DEFAULT_REGRESSION_THRESHOLD_PERCENT, TREND_SIGNIFICANCE_PERCENT, SEVERITY_LADDER, percent_change, classify_severity, classify_change, is_regression, classify_trend, is_meaningful_improvement. MCP's ladder chosen canonical per the approach note; CLI threshold overrides preserved.
work_units.summary: Core policy module with canonical defaults + override hooks

work_units.evidence: compare/report/MCP analytics/database migrated; _classify_regression_severity and _compute_trend_direction deleted. Three-surface parity test over a boundary matrix, plus the exit-code contract tests rung 3 expected but which did not exist. PR #1554.
work_units.summary: Migrate compare/report/MCP analytics; delete local policy constants; three-surface parity test
